source: intelligence/unodc/Stone Keynote for National Dialogue--Final Nov 2023.pdf
speaker: Professor Christopher Stone
summary: Keynote address providing an international perspective on anti-corruption, arguing that systemic integrity requires a combination of internal leadership and external accountability rather than just law enforcement.

key_theses.description: Corruption is inherent in the nature of big power and money, not just an 'infection' by bad individuals.
Daily work of leaders to build internal integrity cultures, sustained by independent external oversight.

critical_observations.description: Digital evidence volume is causing a global decline in police investigations leading to prosecutions; need for world-class digital forensic units in Africa.
Identifying and promoting honest 'corruption resistors' within an institution as a potent tool for culture change.

case_studies.subject: New Orleans Police (USA)
case_studies.lesson: Internal reform without external oversight leads to regression once the individual reformer leaves.

case_studies.subject: Federal Government (Brazil)
case_studies.lesson: Setting uniform standards for ombuds offices, audits, and integrity risk assessments across all departments enables data-driven mentorship for high-risk nodes.
